meta.title: Konabère (Bobo Madaré Nord) Language Ontology
meta.description: A comprehensive ontology of the Konabère language (Bobo Madaré Nord, ISO 639-3: bbo), a Niger-Congo Mande language spoken in Mali and Burkina Faso. This ontology follows the GOLD OntoLing structure with every node fully expanded and populated with Konabère-specific data from all available linguistic sources.
sources: Boone, C.J.L. (2016). Tone in the Bobo Madare North Noun System. Master's thesis, Leiden University.
Coulibaly, N., Diarra, D., Kiénou, D., Wolthuis, W.M.C., Boone, C. (2023). Dictionnaire konabéré-français. SIL International.
Diarra, D., Wolthuis, W. (2017). Guide d'orthographe konabéré. SIL.
Diarra, S., Makeeva, N. (2025). La formation du pluriel des noms en konabéré. Mandenkan 72.
Makeeva, N.V. (2024). Garmoniya glasnykh v yazyke konabere. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana 21.1.
Makeeva, N.V. (forthcoming). Dolgiye glasnyye i diftongi v yazyke konabere.
Prost, A. (1983). Essai de description grammaticale du dialecte bobo de Tansila, Haute-Volta. Mandenkan 5.
Tiendrébéogo, B. (1998). Rapport sociolinguistique sur la langue bobo madaré. SIL/ANTBA.
Wolthuis, W. (2019). Esquisse phonologique du bobo madaré nord (konabéré). SIL International.
meta.classification: Niger-Congo, Mande, Western, North-western, Soninke-Bobo, Bobo
meta.location: Mali (Ségou and Sikasso regions) and Burkina Faso (Banwa province)

Language.definition: Konabère (Kʋ̀nnàbɩ̄rɩ̀) is a Mande language of the Bobo-Samogo group, spoken by approximately 60,000 people in Mali and Burkina Faso. The speakers call themselves Konakuma (sg. Konasun). The name 'konabéré' means 'language of the territory' (kʋ̄ʋ̄ = terrain, nà = genitive/connective particle, bɩ̄rɩ̀ = language).
key_properties: Tonal (3 level tones: H, M, L)

Lexicon.definition: The inventory of sign units (words and morphemes) in Konabère
Lexicon.details: Approximately 7,500+ entries in the Konabère-French dictionary, including nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, postpositions, particles, numerals, and ideophones.

Grammar.definition: The set of rules for operating on these units
Grammar.details: Includes morphological rules (plural formation, derivation, inflection), syntactic rules (SOV word order, postpositional case marking, clause types), and phonological rules (ATR harmony, nasal harmony, tonal rules).

Language.definition: Abstract linguistic system in the minds of speakers
Language.details: 3-level tone system, 9-vowel system with ATR contrast, complete harmonic system, complex plural formation rules.

Speech.definition: The concrete realization of language in communication
Speech.details: Actual spoken forms; dialectal variation between Mafouné (simpler tone system) and Tansila (standard). Fast speech reduction processes (elision of vowels).

Linguistic_System.definition: A term used to describe a language as a whole, with each of its component parts functioning according to an overall convention of usage.
Linguistic_System.konabere_details: Konabère is characterized by a system of 21 consonants, 18 vowels (9 oral + 9 nasal), 3 level tones, ATR harmony, and a unique system of nominal plural formation with over 7 distinct suffix types and multiple vowel alternation patterns.
Linguistic_System.system_of_systems: Konabère can be described as a 'system of systems' with hierarchically ordered levels: phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics. Each level has its own units and rules that interact with other levels.

Linguistic_Taxon.definition: The class of Taxons whose instances are used in the scientific classification of language varieties.
Linguistic_Taxon.konabere_classification: Konabère is classified within the Mande language family, Bobo-Samogo group, Western branch of Mande.

Taxon.definition: The class of scientific categories used to create a taxonomy and determined according to scientific principles in a given domain.
Taxon.konabere_taxonomy: Konabère belongs to the Niger-Congo phylum, Mande family, Western branch, North-western group, Soninke-Bobo sub-group, Bobo-Samogo branch.

Genetic_Taxon.definition: The class of all taxons whose members are based on genetic relatedness.
Genetic_Taxon.konabere_genetic_classification: Konabère is a Niger-Congo language of the Mande family, Western branch, North-western group, Soninke-Bobo sub-group, Bobo-Samogo branch.
Genetic_Taxon.genetic_notes: Dwyer classifies Bobo Madare as an early off-split from the Eastern Mande branch (1989:50, 1994:30).

Context_of_Use_Taxon.definition: The class of taxons whose instances classify language varieties according to how they are primarily used.
konabere_contexts: Literary/Standard: Based on Tansila dialect, used in Bible translation and literacy materials
Daily communication: Used by all generations in all domains of life
Religious: Used in Catholic and Protestant church services
Oral tradition: Used in storytelling, proverbs, and traditional ceremonies

Geographic_Taxon.definition: The class of linguistic taxons whose instances are groupings based on where language varieties are used.
Geographic_Taxon.konabere_geography: Konabère is spoken in Mali (Ségou and Sikasso regions) and Burkina Faso (Banwa province), West Africa.
Geographic_Taxon.area: Approximately 4,200 km² (2,100 km² in Burkina Faso and 2,100 km² in Mali).

Political_Taxon.definition: The class of taxons whose instances are groupings based on political entities.
Political_Taxon.konabere_political_status: Konabère is a cross-border language spoken in both Mali and Burkina Faso. In Mali it is referred to as Konabéré, in Burkina Faso as Bobobéré. It is recognized as a national language for literacy development in both countries.

Endangerment_Taxon.konabere_status: Konabère is listed as 'vigorous' in Ethnologue, with 60,000 speakers and intergenerational transmission. The language is 'unstandardized and in vigorous use among all generations'.
vitality_factors: Literacy programs: Active in multiple locations

Language_Family.definition: Group of languages that are genetically related, i.e., can be traced to a common proto-language.
Language_Family.konabere_family: Mande languages, specifically the Western branch, North-western group, Soninke-Bobo sub-group, Bobo-Samogo branch.

Language_Stock.definition: A term used for postulated but undemonstrated higher-order, more inclusive families.
Language_Stock.konabere_stock: Konabère is part of the Mande stock, which belongs to the Niger-Congo phylum.

Language_Subfamily.definition: A group of languages within a language family which are more closely related to each other than to other languages of that family.
Language_Subfamily.konabere_subfamily: Bobo-Samogo group within Western Mande. Closely related to Southern Bobo Madaré (Sya).

Isolate.definition: A language variety such that there are no other varieties that are genetically related.
Isolate.konabere_isolate_status: Konabère is not an isolate; it has close relatives including Southern Bobo Madaré, Seenku, and other Samogo languages.

Dialect.definition: A regional, temporal or social variety of a language, differing in pronunciation, grammar and vocabulary from the standard language.

konabere_dialects.name: Mafouné
konabere_dialects.notes: Spoken in Mali; somewhat simpler tonal system; base for much of the research data

konabere_dialects.name: Tansila
konabere_dialects.notes: Chosen as standard for literature development; best understood by other speakers; used in Bible translation

Dialect.standard_dialect: Tansila (selected based on sociolinguistic research showing it is the best understood by other Konabère speakers)

The_Linguistic_Sign.definition: A fundamental unit establishing a conventional relation between form and content. An abstract structure whose instances participate in a linguistic system.

Signifier.definition: The external form (sound or written representation)
Signifier.konabere_details: Phonological form including segmental features (consonants, vowels) and suprasegmental features (tone, length).

Signified.konabere_details: Lexical meaning (e.g., sùŋ 'man') and grammatical meaning (e.g., plural marking).

Arbitrariness.definition: No natural relation between signifier and signified
Arbitrariness.konabere_details: Predominantly arbitrary, with some onomatopoeic elements (e.g., popo 'moto', kokori 'coq').

Linear_Character.definition: Elements follow one another in time
Linear_Character.konabere_details: SOV word order; morphemes combine linearly; phonemes occur in sequence.

Double_Articulation.definition: Signs are composed of smaller meaningful signs (primary) and non-meaningful units (secondary)
Double_Articulation.konabere_details: Primary: morphemes (e.g., sɔ̄ŋ-ta 'cultivator' = root + suffix). Secondary: phonemes (e.g., /s/, /ɔ/, /ŋ/).

The_Linguistic_Sign.examples: Words and morphemes are the primary linguistic signs: sùŋ 'man', nàà 'woman', -rèè (plural), -ta (agentive).

Linguistic_Unit.definition: Any entity which constitutes the focus of linguistic enquiry. The unit is the stretch of language that carries grammatical patterns.

Form_Unit.definition: Denotes the sensorily perceptible aspect of the linguistic sign.
Form_Unit.konabere_form: Phonological form including segments (consonants, vowels) and suprasegmental features (tone, length).

Grammar_Unit.definition: The structural component of the linguistic sign and includes notions such as morpheme, syntactic word, and construction.

Semantic_Unit.definition: The class of semantics elements, or units of semantic structure (sometimes called a sememe).

konabere_semantic_units.definition: Meaning of words: sùŋ 'man', kīrì 'village', kimi 'steal'
Meaning expressed by grammatical markers: plural, tense, aspect, mood

Linguistic_Expression.definition: Any physical form (sound, visual image or sequence thereof) used to represent a linguistic unit.

konabere_expressions.Spoken: The physical sound form of Konabère, produced by the vocal apparatus
konabere_expressions.Written: The written physical form of Konabère using the Latin-based alphabet of 30 letters
konabere_expressions.Signed: Not applicable to Konabère; the language is primarily spoken and written

Spoken_Linguistic_Expression.definition: The physical sound form of language as distinct from either signed or spoken expressions.
Spoken_Linguistic_Expression.konabere_spoken: The physical sound form of Konabère produced during a speaking event. Includes all phonetic and tonal variations, dialectal differences, and fast speech processes.

Written_Linguistic_Expression.definition: The written physical form of language as distinct from either signed or spoken expressions.
Written_Linguistic_Expression.konabere_written: The written form of Konabère using the Latin-based alphabet of 30 letters. Standardized orthography based on the Tansila dialect was developed in 2017. The New Testament was published in Konabère in 2020.

Signed_Linguistic_Expression.definition: The signed physical form of language as distinct from either written or spoken expressions.
Signed_Linguistic_Expression.konabere_signed: Not applicable. Konabère is primarily a spoken and written language; no signed variety is documented.

Linguistic_Property.definition: The class of properties that pertain to linguistic units. A unit's properties determine its behavior in a grammatical system.

Linguistic_Data_Structure.definition: An abstract container for grouping together instances of linguistic data, usually to suit a particular theory or computational implementation.

konabere_structures.definition: Dictionary entry with form, meaning, grammatical category, and additional properties
Set of related forms showing inflectional patterns (e.g., singular/plural pairs)
Set of features associated with a linguistic unit (e.g., [ATR=+], [tone=H], [plural_class=Type_I])

Literary_Language.definition: The codified, supra-dialectal, polyfunctional standard form.

Codified.examples: Bible translation (New Testament 2020), dictionaries, literacy materials, formal education.

Territorial_Dialects.definition: Systems functioning in a part of the language's territory

Social_Dialects.definition: Systems used among certain social groups
Social_Dialects.examples: Differences between older and younger speakers; rural vs urban varieties.

Vernacular.definition: Language of non-educated people with deviations from the norm
Vernacular.notes: All varieties of Konabère are used by all education levels; no stigmatized vernacular variety is documented.

Mafouné_dialect.definition: Spoken in Mali, somewhat simpler tonal system, base for much of the research data
Mafouné_dialect.notes: Used in the 2012-2014 research; some tonal differences from Tansila dialect

Tansila_dialect.definition: Spoken in Burkina Faso, chosen as standard for literature development, best understood by other speakers
Tansila_dialect.notes: Used in Bible translation, literacy materials, and the Konabère-French dictionary

Thing.definition: In Web Ontology Language, Thing is the superclass of all classes. The most basic concepts in a domain should correspond to classes that are the roots of various taxonomic trees.
Thing.konabere_thing: In Konabère ontology, Thing is the superclass of all classes. All Konabère linguistic units are instances of Thing.

Abstract.definition: Properties or qualities as distinguished from any particular embodiment of the properties/qualities in a physical medium.
Abstract.konabere_abstract: Grammatical categories in Konabère are abstract: number, tense, aspect, mood, definiteness. These exist independently of any particular spoken utterance.

Object.definition: Corresponds roughly to the class of ordinary objects. Examples include normal physical objects, geographical regions, and locations of processes.
Object.konabere_object: Konabère nouns refer to objects: sùŋ 'man' (human object), kīrì 'village' (location), dibi 'stone' (physical object).

Process.definition: The class of things that happen and have temporal parts or stages. Examples include extended events, actions, and biological processes.
Process.konabere_process: Konabère verbs describe processes, actions, and states: kimi 'steal' (action), nyimi 'dance' (activity), wʊɔ 'cry' (process), ti 'be' (state).

Phonetics.definition: The branch of linguistics studying the sound side of speech communication in Konabère.

Articulatory.definition: Anatomy and physiology of speech production
Articulatory.konabere_details: Study of how Konabère speech sounds are produced using the vocal apparatus.

Acoustic.definition: Physical properties of the sound signal
Acoustic.konabere_details: Study of the acoustic properties of Konabère sounds: formants, fundamental frequency, intensity.

Perceptual.konabere_details: Study of how Konabère sounds are perceived and categorized by native speakers.

Linguistic_Phonetics.definition: Studies the function of sound means in language.
Linguistic_Phonetics.konabere_details: Study of how phonetic features function in the Konabère phonological system to distinguish meaning.

Phonetic_Units.definition: Linear objects that can follow one another in the speech chain.

Segment_Units.definition: Minimal linear units in the speech chain.

types.name: Sound
types.definition: Concrete realization in a specific context

types.name: Sound Type
types.definition: Abstract grouping of phonetically similar sounds

types.name: Phoneme
types.definition: Abstract unit that distinguishes meaning in the language

Suprasegmental_Units.definition: Units consisting of segmental units organized into larger prosodic structures.

Phonetic_Features.definition: Properties characterizing phonetic units in Konabère.

examples: Place of articulation (labial, alveolar, velar, etc.)
Manner of articulation (stop, fricative, nasal, approximant)

Suprasegmental_Features.definition: Features applying to groups of segments

Phonetic_Rules.definition: Rules governing the use and variation of phonetic units in Konabère.

Phonological_Rules.definition: Conscious, regulable rules that are part of the speaker's knowledge
examples: ATR harmony (vowels in a root must share ATR value)
Liquid harmony (/l/ allomorph after roots ending in /l/)

Coarticulatory_Rules.definition: Unconscious, non-controllable rules resulting from articulatory processes
examples: Nasalization of vowels adjacent to nasal consonants
Elision of vowels in rapid speech

notes.p: voiceless stop; not in medial position
notes.b: voiced stop; not in medial position
notes.f: voiceless fricative; rare in medial position
notes.m: nasal; phonemic; predominantly before nasal vowels, limited cases before oral vowels: mɛ̀ɛ̄ 'se coincer', māā 'moudre'

notes.d: voiced stop; rare in medial position; [r] is allophone of /d/ in intervocalic position
notes.n: nasal; allophone of /l/ before nasal vowels
notes.r: vibrant; only in medial position; marginal phoneme

notes.j: affricate; corresponds to /z/ in Southern Bobo
notes.ɲ: nasal; allophone of /y/ before nasal vowels

notes.k: voiceless stop; free variation [k]~[c] before front vowels (i, ɩ, e, ɛ); rare in medial position
notes.g: voiced stop; rare in initial position; can be weakened to [s] between vowels: bāġɩ~bāsi 'planter', dòġɩ~dòsi 'accompagner'
notes.ŋ: nasal; phonemic; can be syllabic; only consonant that can appear in coda position

notes.kp: voiceless labio-velar stop; not in medial position
notes.gb: voiced labio-velar stop; not in medial position
notes.ŋm: labio-velar nasal; allophone of /w/ before nasal vowels; not in medial position

Laryngeal.notes: voiceless fricative; mainly in loanwords; not a phoneme in native words

phonological_notes.g_initial: /g/ is rare in initial position; found in: gani 'world' (3 occurrences in native words), gaabu 'sword', galsura 'saw'
phonological_notes.r_distribution: /r/ is marginal, occurring only in medial position; /d/ is rare in medial position, [r] is allophone of /d/ in intervocalic position
phonological_notes.nasal_allophony: [n], [ɲ], [ŋm] are allophones of /l/, /y/, /w/ respectively before nasalized vowels: lɔ̀ɔ̀ 'poverty' vs. nɔ̰̄ɔ̰̀ 'child'; yaa 'sickle' vs. ɲà̰à̰ 'woman'; wɪɪ 'duration' vs. ŋmɪ̰̀ ɪ̰́ 'razor'
phonological_notes.k_variation: /k/ can be pronounced [k] or [c] before front vowels (i, ɩ, e, ɛ) - free variation: kini ~ cini 'front', kibiri ~ cibiri 'aile'
phonological_notes.g_weakening: Between vowels /g/ is sometimes weakened to [s]: bāġɩ ~ bāsi 'planter', dòġɩ ~ dòsi 'accompagner', dīġɩ ~ dīsi 'plume'
phonological_notes.d-r_allophony: [r] is allophone of /d/ in medial position: tan 's'asseoir' → tanru 'chez' (from *tandu), bee 'vers' → beeru 'vers'

Vowels.definition: 18 vowel phonemes: 9 oral and 9 nasal, with full ATR contrast across all heights

orthographic_representation.oral: i, e, u, o, ɩ, ɛ, ʊ, ɔ, a
orthographic_representation.nasal: in, en, un, on, ɩn, ɛn, ʊn, ɔn, an
orthographic_representation.notes: Nasal vowels are written with a following 'n' (e.g., finin [fĩ] 'troubler', tan [tã] 'vérité')

length_contrast.definition: All vowels can be lengthened; length is phonemic and contrasts with short vowels

Diphthongs.definition: Combinations of two vowels with different qualities within a single syllable
Diphthongs.characteristics: Each diphthong consists of two components with identical values for backness and [ATR]; exceptions include diphthongs with [a] as second component

length_in_diphthongs.definition: Diphthongs can be lengthened; length is realized on the second component

Syllabic_Nasal.definition: 16 words containing a syllabic nasal, representing underlying CV(V) structures where the vowel has been lost through historical reduction
phonetic_characteristics: In 7 words, the syllabic nasal is preceded by a velar plosive
In 4 words, by a homorganic voiceless nasal
The remaining 5 words consist of a syllabic nasal only

analysis.+ATR_nasals: The syllabic nasal with +ATR quality represents the nasalized back closed vowel [u] in velar context
analysis.-ATR_nasals: The syllabic nasal with -ATR quality represents the nasalized back closed vowel [ʊ] in velar context
initial_consonants: For words with [k] or [g] at the surface, the initial consonant is velar
For words with a simple syllabic nasal, the initial consonant is a velar nasal
For the 3 words with a voiceless nasal, the initial consonant is an underlying voiceless fricative (as shown by [s] in the plural)
analysis.bilabial_exception: The word [m] 'ten' has bilabial quality; a labial fricative is posited underlyingly (supported by Southern Bobo cognate [fū])

Syllable.definition: The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Konabère is the mora
evidence: Bimoraic CVCV, CVV, and CVC words have melodies consisting of two tones
Monomoraic CV verbs have one-tone melodies
Each mora carries exactly one tone (except for LML contour which is exceptional)

V.description: Rare; occurs in some personal pronouns (a 'il/elle'), the logophoric pronoun, definite articles (a, i), and demonstratives

CV.description: Most frequent syllable structure; used in predicate markers (auxiliaries), demonstrative pronouns, conjunctions, postpositions, various particles, and fewer than a dozen verbs

CVV.description: Second most frequent syllable structure; can be used as a full word or as one of the syllables in a multisyllabic word

CVN.description: The final consonant is always [ŋ]; about 7% of nouns in tone research have this structure
CVN.distribution: All positions except medial in trisyllabic words

CVVV.description: Often the result of a morphological process; 12 monomorphemic words found

fast_speech_reduction.description: In fast speech, certain words can be contracted
conditions: In disyllabic words, the vowel of the first syllable can be elided if it follows a stop or fricative and precedes a liquid ([l] or [r]) AND if the vowel is [a] or [i]

ATR_Harmony.definition: Konabère has a complete ATR (Advanced Tongue Root) vowel harmony system with both static and dynamic patterns. The [+ATR] feature functions as dominant.
ATR_Harmony.acoustic_correlation: The main acoustic correlate is F1 value: [-ATR] vowels have higher F1 values than their [+ATR] counterparts.
ATR_Harmony.articulatory_description: [-ATR] vowels are produced with: (1) sphincteric constriction of the aryepiglottic folds, (2) tongue root moving backward and downward, (3) larynx raising. [+ATR] vowels are produced with larynx in relaxed position or working to expand the epilaryngeal tube.

static_harmony.definition: Within a root morpheme, vowels must belong to the same ATR set; /a/ is neutral and can combine with both sets
static_harmony.loanword_integration: Loanwords adapt to ATR harmony: ègìlìsi 'église' (< fr. église), misée 'monsieur' (< fr. monsieur), lɛ̀kɛ̀lɩ 'école' (< fr. école)
static_harmony.compounds: Compounds do not require or allow ATR harmonization: yee-tee-naa 'femme qui ramasse les noix de karité'

Rule_1.name: Dynamic Rule 1 (Plural suffix -rV(V))
Rule_1.context: Plural suffix -rV(V) with additive plural meaning
Rule_1.description: Values of [ATR] and rounding spread rightward to the suffixal morpheme containing a non-high vowel
Rule_1.tonal_behavior: The suffix has lexical L tone. When the root ends in H tone, it spreads to the suffix: túú 'forêt' → túú-ró; kúó 'cour' → kúó-róò.

Rule_2.name: Dynamic Rule 2 (Diminutive suffix -lV(V))
Rule_2.description: Values of [ATR] and rounding spread rightward to the suffixal morpheme containing a non-high vowel

Rule_3.name: Dynamic Rule 3 (Plural suffix -V)
Rule_3.description: Values of [ATR] and rounding spread rightward to the suffixal morpheme containing a mid vowel. The final vowel of the root is elided.

Rule_4.name: Dynamic Rule 4 (Plural suffix -li)
Rule_4.description: This is the only dynamic harmony rule that dictates spreading of [ATR] without combination with rounding.

feature_hierarchy.explanation: Rounding harmony affects all [+ATR] vowels and non-high [-ATR] vowels, but not high [-ATR] vowels.

dominance_and_default_values.definition: [+ATR] is the dominant value and [-ATR] is the recessive/default value
evidence: Loanwords take the default [-ATR] allomorph: mīsēē-rēē 'monsieurs', Jàrà-rèè 'les Diarra'

Nasal_Harmony.definition: Nasalization spreads from triggers (nasal consonants and nasalized vowels) to adjacent phonemes, affecting both vowels and consonants

plural_suffix_-rV.condition: When the root ends in a nasalized vowel or velar nasal

plural_suffix_-V.condition: When the root ends in a nasal consonant

plural_suffix_-li.condition: When the root is a diminutive with nasalized final vowel

Liquid_Harmony.definition: Progressive consonant harmony affecting the initial consonant of suffixes -rV(V) and -li
Liquid_Harmony.rule: Allomorph with /l/ appears when the final syllable of the root begins with /l/

Phonological_System.definition: Tone system of Konabère as described in Boone (2016) and Wolthuis (2019)

High (H).definition: Contrastive in nouns and some verbs; in verbs it corresponds in height to mid tone in nouns

Mid (M).definition: Contrastive in nouns; in verbs it corresponds in height to mid tone in nouns

Low (L).definition: Contrastive in both nouns and verbs

notable_absences: MH pattern not found in our data

tone_in_verbs.mapping: Verb low tone corresponds to noun low tone; verb high tone corresponds in height to noun mid tone

automatic_downstep.definition: After a low tone, the next high tone is realized at a lower frequency than an earlier high tone
automatic_downstep.example: Jèlē dúrú párà à kā kúó rɩ̀
automatic_downstep.in_verbs: In the verb system, a mid tone may also undergo downstep

non-automatic_downstep.definition: Tone register is lowered after a floating L tone

upstep.definition: Occasionally a raised or upstepped tone is found; possibly cases of local upstep
upstep.context: Both verb system and noun system

Rule_1.description: Two consecutive L tones cause a preceding M tone to be elevated (MLL → M)
Rule_1.process: Floating M tone added before verb and floating L tone added after verb. Floating M merges with M tone of verb. Floating L tone, in combination with L tone on verb, causes M tone of verb to be raised.
Rule_1.representation: L MML L → L MLL L → L MM

Rule_2.description: A L tone between two M tones merges with the following M tone and causes it to be lowered (MLM → M+M)
Rule_2.representation: L MLM L → L MLM L

Orthographic_System.definition: Standard orthography based on Tansila dialect, developed by Diarra and Wolthuis (2017)
Orthographic_System.letter_list: A a, B b, D d, E e, Ɛ ɛ, F f, G g, Gb gb, H h, I i, Ɩ ɩ, J j, K k, Kp kp, L l, M m, N n, Ŋ ŋ, Ɲ ɲ, Ŋm ŋm, O o, Ɔ ɔ, P p, R r, S s, T t, U u, Ʋ ʊ, W w, Y y

vowel_representation.oral: a, e, ɛ, i, ɩ, o, ɔ, u, ʊ
vowel_representation.distinction: Syllables ending in <n> are open syllables; syllables written with final <ŋ> are closed CVC syllables

marked_tones: á, í (first and second person singular pronouns)
tone_marking.inaccompli_marker: Asterisk (*) before verb indicates inaccompli (action in progress)

examples.accompli: Fanta juo dei. 'Fanta a posé l'eau'

period.name: taa tebunŋ
period.use: Marks a stop at the end of a sentence

interrogation_particles.example: Musa m'a sgu tɛ naa? 'Est-ce Moussa qui a acheté la chèvre?'

Morphology.definition: The branch of linguistics studying the internal structure of words, their forms, and the rules for combining meaningful units in Konabère.
Morphology.key_focus: Identifying patterns of systematic covariation between form and meaning, particularly in complex plural formation and ATR harmony.

Goals.elegant_description: Capture generalizations, not just list facts
Goals.system_external_explanation: Link patterns to factors outside the system

Word.definition: A complex concept with several distinct senses in Konabère

Lexeme.definition: An abstract dictionary word representing a core meaning
types: Compound: sɔ-kālɩ̀ 'tree branch', yee-tee-naa 'shea nut collector'

Word-form.definition: A concrete occurrence of a lexeme in speech

Word_token.definition: A specific occurrence in a text
Word_token.example: The token fúrú in the sentence 'A you fúrú di'

Morpheme.definition: The smallest meaningful (sign) unit; a two-sided unit. Cannot be divided into smaller meaningful parts.
Morpheme.key_properties: Cannot be divided into smaller meaningful parts

Free.definition: Can stand alone as a word

Bound.definition: Cannot stand alone, must attach to another morpheme

Cumulation.definition: Expression of multiple meanings by a single marker
types: Grammatical: plural suffix -rèè also shows ATR harmony
Lexical and Grammatical: -wa marks causative and voice

deviations_from_additive_model.Idiomaticity: Meaning of whole is not derived from parts: yee-tee-naa 'shea nut collector'

Allomorphy.definition: Variation in form of a morpheme
conditioning: Grammatical: plural vs associative plural (-rèè vs -rì)

deviations_from_additive_model.Fusion: Loss of clear boundary between morphemes: vowel change plurals (fúrú → fúró)

types_by_expression.Operational: Modification of another morpheme: vowel alternation

Morph.definition: A concrete, linear realization of a morpheme

examples.-rèè: allomorph of plural suffix after a,e
examples.-nèè: allomorph of plural suffix after nasals

Affix.definition: A morpheme with an abstract meaning which can only be used when added to a root morpheme

Root.definition: The base form of a word which cannot be further analyzed without total loss of identity

examples.bound: sɔ- in compounds (from sùŋ), na- in compounds (from nàà)

Stem.definition: The class of morphological units that are analyzable into a root and possibly one or more derivational units

Three_Forms_of_Nouns.definition: Nouns have three distinct forms: singular, plural, and non-autonomous (used in compounds)

Clitic.definition: A prosodically dependent unit with syntactic freedom

Proclitic.definition: A clitic that precedes the lexical unit

Enclitic.definition: A clitic that is phonologically joined at the end

Compound.definition: A linguistic unit composed of elements that function independently in other circumstances
Compound.structure: First element in non-autonomous form; plural marked on second constituent
Compound.ATR_harmony: Compounds do not require ATR harmonization: yee-tee-naa 'shea nut collector'

Substance_Means.definition: Segmentable units part of the word-form

Inflection.definition: Morphological relationship between word-forms of a single lexeme

Compounding.definition: Combination of two or more lexemes to form a new one

Word_Formation.definition: Cover term for derivation and compounding

Lexicon.definition: The total store of words available to a speaker. Konabère lexicon contains approximately 7,500+ entries.
Lexicon.notes: Konabère lexicon includes nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, postpositions, particles, numerals, and ideophones.

Lexical_Item.definition: A unit of the vocabulary of a language. Konabère lexical items include roots, derived words, and compounds.

Lexicalized_Concept.definition: Grammatical or semantic category expressed by a lexical item. Examples: terms for kinship (tɔŋ 'father', yuo 'mother'), agriculture (dugo 'millet', manɩ 'sorghum').

Inflectional_Paradigm.definition: The complete set of grammatical word-forms of a lexeme
Inflectional_Paradigm.Inflection_Class: Group of lexemes sharing the same set of forms. Konabère has lexically determined plural classes (Types I-IV).
Inflectional_Paradigm.Syncretism: Two or more functions expressed by the same form
Inflectional_Paradigm.Periphrasis: Use of a separate word or phrase

Grammatical_Meaning.definition: Meanings obligatorily expressed by the grammar
Grammatical_Meaning.Grammatical_Category: A set of mutually exclusive, obligatory meanings
Grammatical_Meaning.Grammeme: An individual value within a category

Agreement_Class_Gender.definition: Konabère does not have grammatical gender. Noun classes are based on plural formation patterns (Types I-IV).

Case.definition: Marks syntactic and/or semantic role through postpositions

referential_usage.Definite: Marked by a (SG) or i (PL) before noun

Aspect.definition: Presents situation from internal temporal perspective

Tense.definition: Locates event relative to moment of speech

Inflection_vs_Derivation_Criteria: Relevance to syntax: Inflection is more relevant
Regularity and productivity: Inflection is more regular
Meaning compositionality: Inflection is more compositional
Word class change: Derivation can change class
Position relative to base: Derivation is closer to root

processes: Elision of final vowels in plural forms

Syntax-Morphology_Interface.lexical_integrity: Syntactic rules cannot access internal morphological structure

Morphology_and_Other_Components.Morphology_and_Valence: How morphology affects argument structure: causative -wa adds an agent argument

Productivity.definition: Ability to apply to new bases
restrictions: Semantic: Noun classes are lexically determined
Pragmatic: Some strategies are less productive
Borrowed Vocabulary: Loanwords take default -rèè plural
Productivity.blocking: Existing word prevents formation of synonym

Morphological_Typology.Degree_of_Synthesis: Moderate morpheme-per-word ratio; complex plural formation

Part_Of_Speech_Property.definition: The property that identifies the grammatical class of a word

classes.Noun: Names of entities; take plural and possessive markers
classes.Verb: Actions and states; show TAM distinctions
classes.Adjective: Quality words; relatively small class; plural marked on adjective
classes.Adverb: Modify verbs; often derived from adjectives
classes.Pronoun: Replace nouns; simple, emphatic, and autonomous forms
classes.Postposition: Follow nouns; mark spatial, instrumental, and beneficiary relations
classes.Ideophone: Express sensory impressions; no inherent meaning

Bound_Morpheme.examples: Plural suffixes (-rèè, -nèè, -lì), derivational suffixes (-ta, -pu, -wa), verbal prefixes (ma-, di-)

Inflectional_Morpheme.definition: Express grammatical categories; do not change word class

Derivational_Morpheme.definition: Derive new lexical units; may change word class

Category_Changer.definition: Derivational units that change the syntactic category of the root

Nominalizer.definition: Forms a noun from some other word class

Intransitivizer.definition: Derives an intransitive verb from a transitive verb
Intransitivizer.examples: Vowel change in some verb pairs

Transitivizer.definition: Derives transitive verbs from intransitive verb stems

Copula.definition: Indicates a relationship of equivalency between subject and predicate

Auxiliary.definition: Verbs used in coordination with another verb to express mood, tense or aspect

Modal.definition: Expresses necessity, possibility, attitude toward factuality
Modal.examples: kpin 'can, be able', sebe 'can, be able'

Personal_Pronoun.definition: Refers to speaker, addressee, and others

Demonstrative.definition: Used deictically to indicate spatial, temporal, or discourse location

Quantifier.definition: Expresses definite or indefinite number or amount

Number_Values.Plural: Marked by various suffixes or vowel changes

Tense_Values.Present_Tense: Unmarked; also ti nē + present form for actual present

Mood_Values.Subjunctive: t'a/t'è/t'à + verb; used for wishes and purpose

Case_Property.definition: Grammatical encoding of a noun's relationship to other elements
Case_Property.examples: Nominative (unmarked subject), Accusative (unmarked object), Dative/Locative (postpositions na, ta, di, ma), Genitive (ka with 3rd person)

Evidentiality_Property.definition: Basis for claiming event has occurred

Generative_Grammar.definition: Grammar viewed as a cognitive faculty; language generated by a set of rules

key_assumptions.I-Language: Internal, psychological, cognitive system of grammatical knowledge
key_assumptions.E-Language: External, physical, social manifestation of language
key_assumptions.Performance: Actual use of language, subject to external factors

Basic_Word_Order.example: a junu a sivu kaa a dwu r (3SG AUX 3SG.POSS hand put DEF mouth in) 'She has put her hand into her mouth.'

Postpositions.definition: Function words that follow nouns to indicate case relations

Negation.structure: ma (after subject) ... ko (at end of phrase)
examples: a ma naa ko 'he didn't come'

Interrogation.wh: nɔ at end with interrogative word

Theta_Roles.Theta_Criterion: Each argument assigned one and only one theta role; each theta role assigned to one argument

Constituents.definition: A group of words functioning as a single unit

Noun_Phrase.possessives: Pronoun + ka (3rd person) or pronoun alone (1st/2nd)
Noun_Phrase.adjectives: Follow the noun; plural marked on adjective
Noun_Phrase.numbers: Follow the noun; noun in plural form

Clause_Structure.example: a junu a sivu kaa a dwu r

Declarative.example: a junu a sivu kaa a dwu r
Declarative.negation: a ma junu a sivu kaa a dwu r ko

Interrogative.negative: I naa naa me? 'Isn't it that you're coming?'

Subjunctive.example: Wúrō m'é yié sɔ̄ɔ̄ 'May God lead you!'

Relative_Clause.position: ɲwàn + Noun at beginning of phrase
Relative_Clause.subject: ɲwàn sūn nē fōnō yōō... 'the man who is passing...'
Relative_Clause.object: ɲwàn sūn ē é jàà 'the man I saw'
Relative_Clause.negative: ɲwàn sūn já mẽ bãrã tà 'the man who hasn't worked'

Conditional.example: e ja yɔw Bɔbɔ, e kwia siɔ tee 'if you go to Bobo, buy a bike'

Causal.example: à yōw à wē, à kā tōn sìrì dān yíré nà 'he went home because of his father's death'

Consecutive.example: à gbâà tèè nye nè yòw n' áânè 'he bought a sheep and took it'

Focus.subject: à sēgē nē tùmū 'it's a goat that ran away'
Focus.object: à nānē e n'é yàà 'it's a chicken you killed'

Topicalization.example: ɲwàn sūn nē fōnō yōō, à pānè 'the man who passes there, he's a thief'

Theme_and_Rheme.Theme: Starting point, what sentence is about
Theme_and_Rheme.Rheme: New information, what is said about theme

Agreement.definition: Not overt in Konabère; no subject-verb agreement in person or number

Government.definition: Postpositions determine case marking of noun phrases

Adjunct.definition: A phrase modifying a head but not an actant

Syntactic_Unit.definition: A functional component of a larger construction: constituent, phrase, clause.

Syntactic_Construction.definition: Grammar units with syntactic structure: phrase, clause, sentence.

Syntactic_Word.definition: Lowest position in syntactic construction; largest unit resistant to insertion.

Phrase.definition: Constructions consisting of one or more syntactic words, lacking subject-predicate organization.

Adjective_Phrase.definition: Construction with adjective as head: Adj + (complement).

Semantics.definition: The branch of linguistics studying meaning in Konabère.

Truth-Conditional_Semantics.definition: To know meaning is to know truth-conditions.

Compositionality.definition: Meaning of complex expression determined by meanings of parts and combination rules.

Lexical_Meaning.definition: Meaning of a word as a unit of the lexicon

components.Pragmatic_Component: Conditions of use and speaker's attitude

Polysemy.definition: Single word with multiple related meanings

Grammatical_Meaning.definition: Abstract, obligatory, systematic meaning expressed by grammatical markers

Propositional_Component.Proposition: Set of possible worlds or truth-value
Propositional_Component.Argument_Structure: List of participants with semantic roles

Communicative_Component.Given_New: Information assumed known vs. newly introduced

Pragmatic_Component.definition: Information about speaker's intention and use
Pragmatic_Component.Illocutionary_Force: Type of act (assertion, question, command, wish)

Referential_Status.Definite: Marked by a (SG) or i (PL) before noun: a sùŋ 'the man'
Referential_Status.Indefinite: Unmarked noun; or bɔ 'a, certain': sùŋ bɔ 'a man'

Phonetics-Phonology_Interface.definition: The interaction between the substance of speech (phonetics) and its functional organization in the linguistic system (phonology).
key_areas: Allophonic variation: [k]~[c] before front vowels, [n] as allophone of /l/ before nasal vowels
Phonological rules: ATR harmony, nasal harmony, liquid harmony
Phonetic transcription: Mapping from phonemes to phonetic realization

Phonology-Morphology_Interface.definition: The interaction between sound structure and word structure.
key_areas: ATR harmony in suffixes (plural, diminutive)
Nasal harmony in suffix selection
Liquid harmony in suffix selection
Tone changes in plural formation
Elision of final vowels in plural forms
Compensatory lengthening

Morphology-Syntax_Interface.definition: The interaction between word structure and sentence structure.
key_areas: Lexical Integrity: Syntactic rules cannot access internal morphological structure
Agreement: Konabère lacks overt agreement
Case assignment: Postpositions assign case to noun phrases
Valence changing operations: Causative -wa adds an agent argument

Syntax-Semantics_Interface.definition: The interaction between sentence structure and meaning.
key_areas: Compositionality: Meaning derived from parts and their combination
TAM marking: Tense, aspect, mood express temporal and modal meaning
Focus construction: Fronting for emphasis
Relativization: ɲwàn marks relative clauses
Conditional constructions: ja for real, ta for irreal conditions

Semantics-Pragmatics_Interface.definition: The interaction between literal meaning and context-dependent interpretation.
key_areas: Speech acts: Declaratives, interrogatives, imperatives, wishes
Presupposition: Background information in relative clauses
Definiteness and reference: Marked by a/i articles
Focus and topicalization: Fronting for information structure

subject.definition: Agent of transitive verb or single argument of intransitive verb
subject.example: a sùŋ 'the man' in 'a sùŋ yōw sàyā'

agent.definition: Semantic role of the doer of the action

patient.definition: Semantic role of the undergoer of the action

allomorph.definition: Relation between a morpheme and its allomorphs

allophone.definition: Relation between a phoneme and its phones

realization.definition: Relation between a linguistic unit and its physical form

semanticRole.definition: Relation between a participant and a predicate

argument.definition: The syntactic entity about which something is predicated

inLanguage.definition: Relation between a linguistic sign and Konabère

phoneticRep.definition: Phonetic representation of a linguistic unit

phonemicRep.definition: Phonemic representation of a linguistic unit

orthographicRep.definition: Orthographic representation of a linguistic unit

gloss.definition: Gloss or translation of a linguistic unit

toneMelody.definition: Tonal melody of a noun or verb

pluralClass.definition: Plural class of a noun (Type I-IV)

hasExample.definition: Example usage of a linguistic unit

stringRep.definition: String representation of a linguistic unit

Lexicon_Overview.definition: The lexicon of Konabère includes approximately 7,500+ words and expressions (Coulibaly et al. 2023).
Lexicon_Overview.word_structure: Most words are disyllabic (53%); CV and CVV syllable structures most common.
Lexicon_Overview.loanwords: Primarily from French and Bambara; adapt to ATR harmony and phonotactic constraints.
Lexicon_Overview.noun_classes: Lexically determined plural classes (Types I-IV); not semantically motivated.
Lexicon_Overview.nominal_compounds: Highly productive; plural marked on second constituent.
